harder: One-dribble score counts double; start from a pass so the defender chases on the catch.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Around the Arc (race to the rim)
description: Two players each with a ball dribble around the three-point arc side by side; the leader sets and changes the pace. The moment the leader steps inside the arc, it is a race: first to finish at the rim wins the point. Then swap leader.
coaching_points: Change of pace to gain the first step; long last two steps; finish with either hand.
harder: Bonus point if you make the partner collide with you legally on the way in.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Continuous Chasedown
description: Three attackers with a ball on the perimeter, one defender in the paint. Any attacker may drive at any moment (or the coach calls a name); the defender chases down and contests. After a score or stop the driver sprints to touch the baseline and becomes the defender, the old defender takes her spot outside.
coaching_points: Attack when the defender is not set; defender sprints and contests with the inside hand, no reaching.
harder: Two defenders in the paint; drivers may pass once.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Wing Touchdown (chair pick-up)
description: Defender leads: she speed-dribbles from the wing and places the ball on a chair at the elbow; the attacker sprints to pick it up while the defender turns to recover, then live 1v1. Flip the angle each round.
coaching_points: Pick the ball up with feet ready to attack; defender sprints back to the level of the ball.
harder: Load to 2v2 with a second pair.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Lose the Shadow
description: Two balls on a chair at the top. The attacker moves without the ball trying to lose her shadow (the defender) with changes of speed and fakes; when she gains a step she grabs a ball and it is live 1v1. Great for deception without the ball.
coaching_points: Change speed, not just direction; grab the ball already facing the rim.
easier: Defender shadows at arm's length only.
harder: Attacker must grab the ball with the inside hand and finish in two dribbles.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Elbow Touches
description: Attacker with the ball must touch both elbows of the key with her feet, the defender only the first one, then live 1v1. The extra touch gives the defender a head start so the attacker must beat her with a move.
coaching_points: Attack the recovering defender's front foot; finish through contact.
harder: Limit the attacker to two dribbles.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Five Spots (cone choice)
description: Five cones around the key. The attacker dribbles around any cone she chooses; the defender must go round the opposite way (or trail if it is the top cone), then live 1v1. Add a passer so the attacker receives on the way around the cone and finishes off the catch.
coaching_points: Fake towards one cone, choose another; catch on the move with feet ready.
harder: Load a second defender for 1v2.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Sprint-Ins (rooted defender)
description: Attacker passes to a partner at the top and sprints in, calling for the ball when she wants it back. The defender must stay rooted on or inside the arc and can only react. Live 1v1 after the catch: 3 points for a wide-open finish or a three, 2 for any other rim finish, 1 for mid-range.
coaching_points: Time the call for the return pass; catch on the move; defender walls up early.
easier: Defender must stay in the paint.
harder: Defender may deny the return pass.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Seven Seconds
description: Pass to the attacker starts a 7-second shot clock. Points system: defence 3 for a stop before a shot, 2 for a block, 1 for an air ball; offence 3 for an open lay-up, 2 for a rim finish or a three, 1 for a mid-range make. Play to 10.
coaching_points: Defender sprints out on the pass and contains; attacker decides quickly, no dancing.
harder: Add a help defender who may stunt.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Lane Turns
description: Attacker and defender stay between the lane lines going full length of the key (or half court in a lane). The defender earns a point every time she turns the dribbler, and two bonus points for finishing with a stop and the rebound; nothing if the attacker scores or gets the offensive rebound.
coaching_points: Stay in front, slide, turn the ball; box out after the contest.
harder: Attacker may use the full width of the court.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Protect the Paint (5 seconds)
description: The attacker has 5 seconds to get two feet inside the paint with the ball. The defender scores a point for keeping her out, two for a charge or steal; the attacker one point if she gets in and finishes. Start with no change of direction allowed, then open it up.
coaching_points: Beat the attacker to the spot; chest, not hands; attacker attacks in a straight line first.
harder: Attacker may use counters and step-backs.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Close the Gate (scoring gates)
description: Three cone gates in front of the basket: a wide middle gate and two small side gates, plus the outside. The attacker has 8 seconds: a score through the middle gate is 3 points, through a small gate 2, from outside 1. The defender scores the mirror image for stops.
coaching_points: Defender's job is to close the middle; attacker reads which gate is open.
harder: Add a help defender under the rim.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Open and Chase
description: Defender initiates: she hip-turns and sprints around one side of a cone; the attacker must go around the opposite side and then it is live 1v1, so the defender is always recovering and the attacker learns to attack a chasing defender.
coaching_points: Attacker: go at full speed the moment the defender opens; defender: sprint to get back in front, then contest.
harder: Attacker limited to two dribbles.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 4v4 Prison Break (coach quiz)
description: 4v4 half court with 3x3-style rules. At random the coach calls a defender's name: she runs to the coach and answers a question (a team rule or general knowledge). A wrong answer means she waits 10 seconds — so her team defends 3v4 and must scramble, help and rotate.
coaching_points: Talk and rotate immediately when a teammate leaves; offence attacks the advantage fast.
easier: No penalty for a wrong answer.
harder: Two names called at once.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 1v1 Shuffle Rebounds
description: Attacker shuffles from lane line to lane line; the coach shoots (or throws the ball hard off the backboard). When the ball hits the rim the defender may move and box out but not rebound; live 1v1 for the rebound and put-back.
coaching_points: Find the body, hit and hold, then pursue; attacker crashes from the shuffle.
harder: Add a second attacker crashing from the weak side.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Hot Potato Rebounding
description: Threes: players hand the ball off to each other quickly like a hot potato, weaving around the key. On 'go' whoever holds the ball shoots immediately; the other two fight for the rebound and play until someone scores.
coaching_points: Shoot without hesitation; rebounders find the ball's flight early; go up strong.
harder: Add extra passes or a skip pass before the shot.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Basketball Tennis
description: Pairs 4-5 metres apart with a line as the net. One-hand catch and one-hand pass: the ball must bounce once on the partner's side above knee height; a double bounce is a point. Play sets to 5, then switch hands.
coaching_points: Catch and pass with the same hand; use the wrist; move the feet to the ball.
harder: A dribble combo before each pass; doubles with two balls.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Ping-Pong One-Hand Passes (60 s)
description: Passer keeps a sideways dribble; a receiver in the corner signals with hands and eyes and the passer fires a one-hand pass off the dribble while a blocker in between tries to get two hands on the ball. A pass right into the target is a point; 60-second bursts, then rotate.
coaching_points: Pass off the dribble without gathering; put the ball where the target hands are.
harder: Pass with the weak hand only.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Grid Passing 1v1+1
description: Four cones in a square, receiver and defender start in the middle, passer outside. The receiver may only catch while standing on one of the four cones, so she must seal the defender and show hands and eyes to say where she wants the ball. Rotate every 30 seconds.
coaching_points: Body between defender and ball, hands as a target, call for it; passer fakes.
harder: Add a defender on the passer; play 2v2 live after the catch.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Make a Lead (pass into space)
description: Receiver in the middle, a cone on each side, defender behind her. The defender touches one cone; the receiver must move to the opposite cone while the passer dribbles towards the defender's side and delivers a one-hand pass into the space, weighted for the runner.
coaching_points: Pass to where the receiver will be, not where she is; weight the pass.
harder: Add a defender on the passer; finish with a lay-up.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Rapid-Fire Partner Passing (first to 12)
description: Pairs race to complete 12 passes of the type called: chest, bounce, one-hand push, hook, off the dribble, wrap-around. First pair to 12 wins the round; a dropped ball resets.
coaching_points: Accuracy first, then speed; ready hands every pass.
harder: Weak hand only; alternate pass types each pass.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 2v1 Break the Line
description: Passer, defender and receiver in a straight line. The passer cannot pass until the defender has closed out and touched the ball; the receiver must move to break the line and receive a clean pass. On a steal or deflection play live 1v1 or 2v1 to the basket.
coaching_points: Receiver: one step to create an angle, hands ready; passer: pivot and fake before passing.
harder: Passer may only use one hand.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 2v2 Bowling Strikes
description: Three cones as pins guarded by two defenders; two attackers pass (no dribbling) and use fakes to find a gap and throw the ball at the pins. A knocked cone is a strike. 60-second bursts, then swap roles.
coaching_points: Fake a pass to make a pass; defenders move on the flight of the ball.
easier: Attackers may take two steps with the ball.
harder: Weak hand only; a no-look strike counts double.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 3v3 Touchdown (passing only)
description: 3v3 full court, no dribbling. Score a touchdown by catching the ball behind the opponents' baseline. If the ball carrier is tagged she must put the ball down exactly where she was tagged and the other team takes over.
coaching_points: Move immediately after passing; lead the runner; talk on defence.
easier: Allow two steps with the ball.
harder: Weak-hand passes only; a baseline-to-baseline pass counts double.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 4v2 Rondo
description: Four passers on the corners of a square, two defenders inside. Eight passes in a row is a point; a defender who deflects or tags the ball holder swaps out with the passer who lost it. Variations: call the receiver's name before passing, no-look passes only, one dribble then one-hand pass.
coaching_points: Fake, then pass away from the defender's hands; see the second defender.
harder: Passers may not move their feet; one dribble allowed then a one-hand pass.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Pass Tag
description: One team has the ball and tries to tag every opponent with it (touch, not throw). The holder may take only one step and may not dribble, so the team must pass quickly to trap runners. Time how long it takes to get everyone out, then swap.
coaching_points: Pass ahead to a teammate closer to the runner; runners spread out.
harder: Two balls in play.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Hunter Tag (ball holder is safe)
equipment: 1 ball per group of 3-4 (two balls for 5-6)
description: Groups of 3 to 6 with one ball (two balls for larger groups). The hunter may only tag a player who does not have the ball, so the group keeps passing to whoever is about to be tagged. Tagged player becomes the hunter.
coaching_points: Call for the ball early; pass before the hunter arrives; catch with two hands.
harder: Bounce passes only.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 3v3 Rugby (dribble forward, pass back)
description: 3v3 full court with one rule: you may dribble forward but every pass must go backwards (towards your own basket). Score at the far basket. Forces the ball handler to attack and teammates to trail in support.
coaching_points: Attack the space in front with the dribble; trailers fill behind at an angle; defence stops the ball first.
harder: Play 4v4 or 5v5 with the same rule.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Animals Game 4v4 (one defender starts ahead)
description: 4v4 full court, but one defender may only start in her own front court, so the offence brings the ball up 4v3 and must score before the ball crosses half court and the fourth defender joins. Variations: passing only in the backcourt; only one off-ball player inside the arc.
coaching_points: Recognise the advantage and attack it early; pass ahead; the late defender sprints to the ball.
easier: Late defender waits for the first pass in the front court.
harder: No dribble in the backcourt.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Circle Touch (temporary advantage)
description: Play 2v2 to 4v4. When the ball crosses half court, one defender (coach's call) must run and touch the centre circle before recovering, so the offence has an advantage for a few seconds and must score before it disappears. On a stop the defence transitions and two new defenders join.
coaching_points: Read the advantage and attack it fast; touch and sprint back for the defender.
harder: Turnover if the offence does not score during the advantage.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Spacing Races
description: Two teams weave around the key. The coach calls a spacing pattern — 4-out empty, 4-out filled, 5-out — and each team must sprint down the floor and self-organise into that pattern at the far end. First team correctly set wins the point.
coaching_points: Talk and point; fill the corners first; everyone stops on a spot.
harder: Add a ball that must be reversed once the pattern is set.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Breakout and Baseball (kick-ahead)
description: Pairs: one rebounds off the board, takes one breakout dribble and throws a long kick-ahead (baseball) pass to the partner who took off on the rebound. A pass caught in rhythm is a point; first to 4, then swap.
coaching_points: Rebound, chin, one dribble to clear, throw ahead of the runner; runner sprints wide.
easier: Two dribbles; partner waits at half court.
harder: Add a defender contesting the breakout or the finish.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: 3v3 Three Stages
description: Two teams race through three stages at one basket. Stage 1: three passes in a row inside the paint with no dribbles (screen, seal, pivot). Stage 2: score inside the arc only off a cut or a screen. Stage 3: score off a called two-player action. A steal means the other team plays whichever stage they are on.
coaching_points: Coach the stage they are on; celebrate clean cuts and screens, not just baskets.
harder: Shot clock per stage.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Charger (three teams, first to 11)
description: Three teams, one waiting at half court. After a made basket the scoring team stays, the defence sprints off and the waiting team touches the centre circle before sprinting on to defend. First to 11 with the team scoring system (open lay-up 5, mid-range 1, +1 for scoring within 6 seconds, +1 after an offensive rebound). Play 3v3, 4v4 or 5v5.
coaching_points: Sprint back on every change; the incoming team communicates match-ups on the run.
harder: Game over for a team that does not run back after a turnover.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Cambio (change baskets on the call)
description: 3v3 or 4v4 played sideline to sideline between two side baskets (or on one half court). When the coach calls 'cambio' the attacking team must immediately switch to the other basket and keep playing. Constraints per round: left hand only, no dribble, scores only after a skip pass.
coaching_points: Re-space instantly after the call; defence sprints to protect the new basket first.
harder: Cambio can be called several times a possession.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Floor Is Lava (catch only in the paint or beyond the arc)
description: Normal 3v3 to 5v5 half court with one rule: a player may receive the ball only on a cut inside the paint or while standing outside the three-point line — the mid-range is lava. Forces spacing and hard cuts.
coaching_points: Space to the arc, cut to the rim, nothing in between; passers fake and hit the cutter early.
easier: Lava only after the second pass.
harder: Scores from the paint count double.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Scramble Touch (name called, possession changes)
description: 3v3 half court. At any moment the coach calls a player's name: possession changes to the other team and the player who had the ball must touch the half-court line before recovering on defence, so her team scrambles 2v3 for a few seconds.
coaching_points: Defence: talk and cover the most dangerous player first; offence: attack the scramble immediately.
easier: Name called only on a dead ball.
harder: Two names called.
source: Transforming Basketball — Small-Sided Games Book (transformingbball.com), adapted

name: Dribble and Toss (tennis ball)
description: Dribble the basketball with one hand while tossing and catching a tennis ball with the other: toss and catch, toss-clap-catch, toss under the leg, toss high while switching the dribble hand. Then walking, then jogging. Count how many catches in a row without losing either ball.
coaching_points: Eyes on the tennis ball, feel the basketball; keep the dribble low and steady.
harder: Weak-hand dribble; two tennis balls; partner throws the tennis ball to you.

name: Tennis Ball Wall Reaction
description: Two metres from the wall: throw the tennis ball against the wall and catch it with one hand, then the other, then after one bounce, then with a clap in between, then turn 180 degrees and catch. In pairs one throws and the other catches the rebound off the wall.
coaching_points: Ready position with the hands up; move the feet to the ball; catch with soft fingers.
harder: Two tennis balls alternating; catch while dribbling a basketball.

name: Tennis Ball Tag and Catch
description: Everyone jogs around the half court tossing and catching their own tennis ball. On the whistle the coach calls a task: freeze and balance the ball on the back of the hand, swap balls with the nearest player by throwing, sit down and stand up without dropping it, or a two-player race to a line.
coaching_points: Head up while jogging; quick reaction to the call.
harder: Dribble a basketball at the same time.

name: Tennis Ball Juggle Progression
description: One ball: toss from hand to hand in an arc at eye level. Two balls: toss one, when it peaks toss the other, catch both (the two-ball exchange). Three balls for those who can. Count consecutive catches; try it standing on one leg.
coaching_points: Throw to the same height every time; eyes on the peak, not the hands.
easier: Beanbags or scarves instead of balls.
harder: Juggle two balls with one hand; juggle while walking.

name: Keep the Balloon Up (dribbling)
description: Keep a balloon in the air with one hand while dribbling a basketball with the other. Count the taps; then tap only with the head, elbow or knee; then walk while doing it; in pairs share one balloon and alternate taps.
coaching_points: Small taps keep the balloon close; the dribble stays automatic and low.
harder: Weak-hand dribble; two balloons per pair.

name: Balloon Volley Pairs
description: Pairs volley a balloon over a cone line: one touch each, then two touches, then only with the non-dominant hand, then both players dribble a basketball while volleying. First pair to 20 volleys wins.
coaching_points: Move under the balloon with the feet before hitting it.
harder: Balloon must be hit with a jump.

name: Balloon Team Keep-Up
description: Teams of 4-5 in a circle keep one balloon in the air; a player may not touch it twice in a row and must sit down and stand up after each touch. Count the touches before it drops; then add a second balloon; then everyone dribbles a basketball.
coaching_points: Call your touch; cover the space left when a teammate sits.
harder: Two balloons and only weak-hand touches.

name: Balloon Relay Race
description: Relay to a cone and back carrying the balloon: between the knees, on the back of the hand, tapped in the air the whole way, then dribbling a basketball with the other hand while tapping. A dropped balloon means restart from the last cone.
coaching_points: Control before speed; cheer the teammate.
harder: Two balloons at once.

name: Stick Drop Reaction
description: Partner holds a wooden stick upright with a fingertip and lets it go without warning; the player in athletic stance must catch it before it hits the floor. Increase the distance step by step; then start from a slide, then from a jump, then facing away and reacting to 'go'.
coaching_points: Athletic stance, weight on the balls of the feet, explode with the first step.
harder: Two sticks, partner drops one; catch with the hand the partner calls.

name: Stick Circle Exchange
description: Group in a circle, everyone holds a stick upright on the floor with one finger. On 'go' everyone lets go and moves one place to the right to catch the next stick before it falls. Widen the circle as they succeed; call left or right; call 'two' to skip a stick.
coaching_points: Release and move at the same time; low, quick steps.
easier: Small circle, always the same direction.
harder: Sticks released on a visual signal; move through the middle of the circle.

name: Stick Balance and Agility
description: Balance the stick upright on the palm and walk; then on two fingers; then on the back of the hand. Then sticks on the floor as an agility pattern: hop over each, in-and-out, sideways two-foot jumps, lateral quick steps between them.
coaching_points: Eyes on the top of the stick to balance it; quiet feet on the pattern.
harder: Balance while dribbling a basketball with the other hand.

name: Stick Pass Relay
description: Teams in a line. Run to the cone carrying the stick balanced on the palm, hand it to the next player; then run holding it like a torch and jump over a cone; then two players carry it between them on the back of their hands without dropping it.
coaching_points: Slow is smooth; pass the stick with eye contact.
harder: Balance the stick while dribbling.

name: Bumper Cars (contact dribbling)
description: Everyone dribbles inside a marked square. Players bump shoulder to shoulder with whoever they meet — gently, like bumper cars — while keeping the dribble alive. Losing the ball means 3 crossovers outside and back in. Shrink the square every minute.
coaching_points: Low and wide stance before contact; ball on the far hand; bump with the shoulder, never the hands.
harder: Weak hand only; a bumped player who loses the ball becomes a tagger.

name: Sumo Circle (hold your ground)
description: Pairs face each other inside a small circle in athletic stance, hands on each other's shoulders (or palms together). On 'go' each tries to push the partner out of the circle or make her move a foot. Best of three, then change partner. Older players do it back to back like a box-out.
coaching_points: Feet wider than the shoulders, hips low, push with the legs not the arms.
easier: Palms only, no pushing on the shoulders.
harder: Back to back: sit into the partner and hold the position for 5 seconds.

name: Rebound Rumble (U9 box-out game)
description: Pairs under the basket. The coach tosses the ball high off the backboard; before it comes down each player tries to get her body between the partner and the ball, turning and sitting into her (no pushing with the arms). Whoever catches it scores a point and gets a lay-up. First to 5.
coaching_points: Turn, find the partner with your back, then look for the ball; catch with two hands.
easier: Coach places the ball on the floor: first to secure it wins.
harder: Three players: the one who rebounds attacks 1v2.

name: Push-the-Pad Finishes
equipment: blocking pad or a rolled mat, balls
description: Lay-up line where the coach (or a player) holds a pad in the lane and gives a gentle bump as the shooter goes up. A made lay-up through the bump is 2 points, a miss with balance kept is 1. Team race to 20.
coaching_points: Two-foot power step, ball at the chin, go up through the bump.
harder: Bump from the side, then from behind; finish with the weak hand.

name: Closeout and Contest Race
description: Two lines under the basket, two shooters on the wings. Coach passes to one wing: the first defender sprints, chops the feet and contests with a high hand; the shooter shoots on the catch. Defence gets a point for a miss, offence for a make; a foul is 2 for the offence. First team to 10, then rotate.
coaching_points: Sprint half way, short choppy steps the second half; hand up, not out; land balanced.
harder: Shooter may shot-fake and take one dribble; defender must contain.

name: 2v2 Closeout and Help
description: Two defenders start in the paint, two attackers on the wings. Coach passes to a wing: the near defender closes out, the other jumps to help position. The attacker drives or swings the ball; the defence must close out again and help and recover. Live to a score or a stop, then rotate.
coaching_points: Close out under control; help defender sees ball and player; recover on the pass, not after the shot.
harder: Add a third attacker in the corner.

name: Closeout Decision Game (shot or drive)
description: Defender under the rim passes to the attacker at the wing and closes out. The attacker reads the closeout: shoots if the defender is short, drives the front foot if she flies past. One dribble maximum. Points: stop 2, contested miss 1, attacker score 2. Winner stays on defence.
coaching_points: Defender: closeout depth depends on the shooter; attacker: read the feet, decide before the catch.
harder: Two dribbles and a help defender.

name: Closeout Tag (sprint and chop)
description: Attackers stand on the arc, defenders in the paint. On the whistle every defender sprints to an attacker and must stop in a chopped-feet closeout stance one arm's length away, hand up; the attacker then takes one step in any direction and the defender must slide to stay in front. Points for each clean closeout, then swap.
coaching_points: Sprint then chop; weight back, hand high; slide without crossing the feet.
harder: Attackers move as the defender arrives.

name: Offensive Rebound Tip Game
description: Coach shoots to miss; one defender boxes out, one attacker crashes from the wing. If the attacker gets the ball she must score immediately with a tip or a power move; the defender must rebound and outlet to the coach. Points both ways, first to 5, then rotate.
coaching_points: Attacker: swim or spin past the box-out, go up strong; defender: hit first, then find the ball.
easier: Attacker starts closer to the basket.
harder: 2v2 crash and box-out.

name: War Rebounding 3v3 (three chances)
description: 3v3 around the key, coach shoots. Live until the defence secures the rebound and outlets, or the offence scores; the offence may go for three offensive rebounds in a row. Defence point for the outlet, offence point for a put-back. First to 7, then switch.
coaching_points: Box out on the shot every time; pursue with two hands; chin the ball and pivot away from pressure.
harder: A stop only counts if the outlet pass is completed within 3 seconds.

name: Box-Out Circle Game
description: Ball in the middle of a circle (centre circle or cones). Defenders face out with attackers behind them. On 'go' the attackers try to touch the ball, the defenders box them out for 5 seconds. Point for the defence if nobody touches it. Then swap.
coaching_points: Turn, make contact with the hip, arms wide, feet moving; hold for the full count.
harder: Two balls in the circle; defenders start facing the attacker.
